Security ecosystem

Security work connects discovery, investigation, approved action, and learning. Explore how those disciplines fit together in the CyberHiveX approach.

01Conceptual architecture

Context to action, with review built in.

A workflow overview. Actual data sources, integrations, and action permissions are defined for each deployment.

  1. 01

    Collect context

    Approved asset information, relevant security logs, and threat context.

  2. 02

    Investigate

    Rakshak AI supports organizing signals and investigation priorities.

  3. 03

    Review & decide

    Analysts examine evidence and agree on the appropriate next action.

  4. 04

    Act & improve

    Approved changes, documented results, and lessons for the next review.

02Explore the lifecycle

Eight stages. One continuous review.

Choose a stage to inspect its inputs, review activities, and expected working output. Use arrow keys to move between stages.

Stage 01 / Discover

Build an agreed picture of your assets.

Establish the systems, services, and owners in scope. Record gaps and uncertain ownership before treating discovered assets as part of the environment.

Review activities

  • Review public-facing assets
  • Reconcile cloud and application inventories
  • Confirm ownership and exclusions

Input

Approved asset scope and available inventory

Working output

An inventory with ownership and review gaps

03Working principles

Visibility, evidence, ownership.

Know the scope

Start with assets, permissions, and responsibilities. Active testing requires explicit authorization.

Keep evidence visible

Show the source, limitations, and reasoning behind a finding or proposed action.

Close the review loop

Document decisions, verify agreed changes, and revisit the workflow as requirements evolve.
